title: RAW UNREVIEWED: Benedict39: a second meal partitions the existing daily bread allowance rather than duplicating it
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED_NOT_SELECTED_NOT_TESTED. One daily bread allowance applies whether there is one meal or two; with supper, the cellarer retains a third of that same allowance for later service. Preserve one quantity across reservation and delivery, while retaining the chapter’s separate alternatives and exceptions.

differentiating_relation: DAILY_AMOUNT is shared by MEAL1 and optional MEAL2; if MEAL2 is scheduled, PART_OF(DAILY_AMOUNT, one-third) is RESERVED and later SERVED to the recipients. The second meal changes timing/partition, not the default daily total.
complete_source_account: Two cooked dishes allow a person unable to eat one to take the other; a third dish depends on additional produce being available.
The bread default is one daily pound, with a third of that same amount held for supper when there are two meals.
The abbot may add food for heavier work; younger boys receive less; the weak and sick are excepted from the quadruped-flesh restriction.
known_counterexplanation: A per-meal allowance reading doubles the daily bread when supper occurs. A newly supplied supper portion loses the explicit part-of relation. A universal fixed-quantity reading contradicts the work and age exceptions retained in the same chapter.
